necessary_conditions.literal: In the rest of the paper all varieties and birational maps between them are defined over C.
necessary_conditions.scope: everything after the introduction is over C; the field-automorphism formulas of Section 1.2 (lines 160-170) are stated for a general field k, but the theorems are over C

necessary_conditions.item: Y is P^3 or a smooth cubic threefold
necessary_conditions.literal: Throughout this section, Y will denote either P^3 or a smooth cubic 3-fold in P^4.
necessary_conditions.scope: Sections 3-4; the two cases have different (g,d) lists and different automorphism groups, so no result may be transferred silently between them

necessary_conditions.literal: Denote by H^Y_{g,d} the Hilbert scheme of subvarieties of Y with Hilbert polynomial P(n) = dn - g + 1.
necessary_conditions.scope: fixes the meaning of (g,d); S^Y_{g,d} is one irreducible component, not the whole Hilbert scheme
only these six pairs are covered by Proposition 3.1 and therefore by every downstream claim

necessary_conditions.literal: there exists an irreducible component S^Y_{g,d} of H^Y_{g,d} whose general element C is a smooth curve satisfying the following
necessary_conditions.scope: chi_C is constructed only for a general element of the component

necessary_conditions.item: X is the blowup along C
necessary_conditions.literal: if X -> Y is the blowup of Y along C
necessary_conditions.scope: Proposition 3.1, Proposition 3.4, Proposition 3.5 and Corollary 3.6 all assume X is this blowup

necessary_conditions.item: weak Fano and free anti-canonical system
necessary_conditions.literal: X is a smooth weak-Fano 3-fold, there are finitely many (-K_X)-trivial curves and |-K_X| is base-point free
necessary_conditions.scope: item (prop:i) of Proposition 3.1; this is the input that Proposition 3.5 and both Case 3 diagrams rely on

necessary_conditions.literal: The anti-canonical model Z := Proj(...) of X is a sextic double solid, that is a double cover of P^3 ramified along a sextic hypersurface.
necessary_conditions.scope: item (prop:ii); Z and its deck transformation p are what define chi_C in Remark 3.2

necessary_conditions.item: chi_C is defined through eta and p
necessary_conditions.literal: denote by eta the rational map Y --> X -> Z and by p the deck transformation of Z over P^3. Then chi_C := eta^{-1} o p o eta : Y --> Y defines a birational map. Note that chi_C is an involution.
necessary_conditions.scope: the involution property is asserted without proof in the remark; it is not upgraded to an author-proved statement here

necessary_conditions.literal: A morphism eta : X -> B is a rank r fibration if: (def:1) X/B is a relative Mori Dream Space; (def:2) dim X > dim B and rho(X/B) = r; (def:3) X is Q-factorial and terminal and any output of a D-MMP over B is still Q-factorial and terminal; (def:4) there is an effective Q-divisor Delta_B with (B,Delta_B) klt; (def:5) the anticanonical divisor of X is eta-big.
necessary_conditions.scope: all five conditions are used, and Corollary 3.6 uses def:3 for W and def:1 for W'

necessary_conditions.literal: A trivial relation is one of the forms phi^{-1} = psi and alpha o phi o beta = psi ... An elementary relation is one that arises from a rank 3 fibration
necessary_conditions.scope: the whole rigidity claim is 'no non-trivial elementary relation', i.e. excluding elementary relations, not all relations

necessary_conditions.literal: we will say that two Sarkisov links phi and psi are equivalent if there exist alpha, beta, isomorphisms of Mori fiber spaces such that alpha o phi o beta = psi
necessary_conditions.scope: the quotients used to define the index sets I and J and the assignment in Theorem 4.2 are taken up to this equivalence, not up to Bir(Y)-conjugacy

necessary_conditions.literal: (chi_C)^2 = id and a o chi_C o b o psi^{-1} = id, where a, b^{-1} are any Mori fiber space isomorphisms starting from Y
necessary_conditions.scope: these two are exactly the relators that Theorem 4.2 must send to the neutral element and Theorem 4.8 must absorb

quantifier_and_regularity_points.note: smoothness is what lets Proposition 3.5 invoke the contraction classification with W terminal and X smooth

quantifier_and_regularity_points.literal: pi : (W,E) -> (X,z) be a divisorial contraction with W Q-factorial and terminal
quantifier_and_regularity_points.note: the conclusion '-K_W is not big' is asserted only under these two conditions, and Case 1 additionally needs a,b coprime (line 556)

quantifier_and_regularity_points.literal: a (1,a,b)-blowup of a point, with a,b coprime
quantifier_and_regularity_points.note: the inequality (a+b)^2/(ab) > 2 used in Case 1 is stated for coprime positive a,b

quantifier_and_regularity_points.literal: We distinguish 3 cases based on the geometry of the center z
quantifier_and_regularity_points.note: z a point; z a curve not contracted by X -> Z; z a curve contracted by X -> Z. The exhaustiveness is the author's claim, taken as written

quantifier_and_regularity_points.literal: By [AutosOfHypersurfaces] Aut(Y) is finite and so is G.
quantifier_and_regularity_points.note: the finiteness of the automorphism group of a smooth cubic threefold is a cited input, not reproved

quantifier_and_regularity_points.point: G is the set of non-identity automorphisms
quantifier_and_regularity_points.note: R and hence F is a finite union over the non-identity elements; the identity is excluded deliberately

quantifier_and_regularity_points.literal: I_{g,d} is the set of elements of S^Y_{g,d} up to automorphisms of Y ... J_{g,d}^Y is the set of elements of S^Y_{g,d} that are fixed by no non-trivial automorphism of Y, up to projective equivalence
quantifier_and_regularity_points.note: I quotients by Aut(Y); J quotients by projective equivalence and additionally imposes the fixed-point-free condition. The two quotients are not the same and must not be merged

quantifier_and_regularity_points.literal: there exists j_0 in J_{g,d}^Y with j_0' := rho(j_0) in J_{g',d'}^Y and (g,d) != (g',d')
quantifier_and_regularity_points.note: this is essential: the non-inner conclusion compares genera, so the permutation cannot stay inside one (g,d)

quantifier_and_regularity_points.literal: the order of phi(rho) is equal to the order of rho and since J is infinite we can find permutations of any order
quantifier_and_regularity_points.note: the 'arbitrary order' claim depends on J being infinite (not merely non-empty) and on rho being realisable as a permutation of J

quantifier_and_regularity_points.literal: for Theorem 3 the action of a field automorphism tau on Aut(Bir_C(Y)) is well-defined if and only if tau preserves Y, that is a_tau(Y) = Y
quantifier_and_regularity_points.note: the cubic-threefold version of the non-generation statement is explicitly restricted to field automorphisms preserving Y
intro clause of Theorem 1, matched in the body proof by mapping all links not equivalent to some chi_{C_i} to the neutral element (line 699)

quantifier_and_regularity_points.literal: there exist elements chi_i in Cr_3(C), i in I, of degree 19 not in the kernel
quantifier_and_regularity_points.note: degree 19 is the (14,11) P^3 entry of the degree table at line 542; for the cubic threefold the minimum is 11 (line 546)

author_unexpanded_or_open_scope.literal: Note that chi_C is an involution.
author_unexpanded_or_open_scope.state: asserted in a remark, no proof given; status preserved as author assertion

author_unexpanded_or_open_scope.literal: However we expect the statement of Lemma 4.5 to be true for them as well: using a degeneration argument this amounts to just exhibiting one such curve with no projective automorphisms.
author_unexpanded_or_open_scope.state: explicitly an expectation, not a proved result; no degeneration is carried out in the paper

author_unexpanded_or_open_scope.item: extension to other Fano threefold involutions
author_unexpanded_or_open_scope.literal: among the lists of [Cutrone-Marshburn] there are several other examples of involutions of Fano 3-folds which have the same property. Thus it is a natural question whether the whole construction extends to these cases as well.
author_unexpanded_or_open_scope.state: open question posed in the closing subsection; nothing is proved about those cases

author_unexpanded_or_open_scope.literal: For the non-emptiness of S^Y_{g,d} we refer to [WeakFanos, Sec. 5.1] and [WeakFanosCubics, Sec. 3.3] ... the proof of (prop:i) can be found in [WeakFanos, Prop. 5.11] and [WeakFanosCubics, Prop. 3.7]
author_unexpanded_or_open_scope.state: external citations, accepted at the author's stated granularity; not reproved and not certified here

author_unexpanded_or_open_scope.item: first part of Theorem 2.7 and its isomorphisms
author_unexpanded_or_open_scope.literal: The first part of the theorem is due to [HM13]. The original version does not mention the isomorphisms of Mori fiber spaces, which are however implicit in their proof.
author_unexpanded_or_open_scope.state: the author notes the cited theorem is slightly weaker than what is used; this is flagged but not repaired by this session

author_unexpanded_or_open_scope.item: klt-ness of the base in the rank 2 correspondence
author_unexpanded_or_open_scope.literal: Finally, the fact that B is klt is proved in [Fujino, Cor. 4.6].
author_unexpanded_or_open_scope.state: external citation inside a sketch remark; not expanded

no_certification_note: This file records source locations and literal phenomena only. No endpoint, hypothesis or derivation was added or repaired, and no claim of mathematical correctness is made for the author's arguments or for the cited literature.

producer_core_recount_boundaries.note: Proposition 3.5 plus its three cases is the geometric core; Lemmas 2.10 and 2.11 are local computations supporting Case 1 and are not counted separately; Corollary 3.6, Theorem 4.2 and Theorem 4.8 consume C1 and are not recounted

Lemma 4.4 is a general tool and is not counted on its own; Lemma 4.5 counts once with both its (2,8) and (6,9) sub-cases, since they share the same conclusion and only differ in the very-ampleness verification
Lemma 4.7 is not the same unit as C2: different ambient variety and a different exclusion mechanism

Theorem 4.2, Theorem 4.8, Proposition 4.10 and Corollary 4.11 are standard free-product / relator / base-locus arguments after C1, C2, C3 and the cited Theorem 2.7; they are not counted as new advanced units even though they are the paper's headline results

existence and item (prop:i) are delegated verbatim to WeakFanos and WeakFanosCubics; item (prop:ii) is a degree-by-degree computation of h^0(-nK_X) with HRR and Kawamata-Viehweg. The computation is the author's but it is a routine verification once (-K_X)^3 = 2 and base-point-freeness are granted
deg chi_C = (r^2 H^3 - d)r - 1 follows from a 2x2 matrix on N^1 with entries fixed by phi^2 = id; short and standard
the dimension estimate is a normal-bundle-sequence count with Serre duality vanishing for the six specific pairs; it establishes uncountability of I but introduces no new mechanism

Theorems 1, 2, 3 print in the independent introductiontheorem counter and are restatements of Theorem 4.2, Theorem 4.8, and Proposition 4.10 with Corollary 4.11 respectively; only the body results carry material
